messages:
Samir: Heads-up — found an SDK vs REST parity issue while testing the onboarding sample app.
Elyse: what happened?
Samir: SDK call to `redwood.chat.create()` is dropping `client_meta` when we proxy through the frontend helper. REST accepts it fine. Repro steps: hit REST /v1/chat with body containing `client_meta` -> works. Call SDK method with same payload -> server-side logs show no `client_meta`.
Aj: is this the same `client_meta` used for routing -> dedicated vs hosted?
Samir: yes, it affects routing policy and also a retry header we rely on. If `client_meta` missing, requests fall back to lower-priority pool and we see higher latencies + more failures.
Kevin: omg that explains the weird canary traffic we saw this morning. ci-bot build triggered a test that uses the sample app and timed out.
ci-bot: [automation] integration-test/sample-onboarding failed (timeout) — see CI job 4521
Elyse: any idea where the stripping happens? frontend or SDK shim?
Samir: quick bisect — the browser helper (redwood-js) serializes `options` and does `JSON.stringify(options)` but later reconstructs a subset for security; `client_meta` not whitelisted. REST bypasses that so it's preserved.
Aj: should we add `client_meta` to whitelist or change the SDK to forward unknown keys into metadata envelope?
Elyse: whitelist is easiest short-term but brittle. Forwarding unknown keys might leak stuff. We need a clear contract.
Kevin: also noticed streaming mismatch: REST streams partial tokens as they arrive; SDK buffers and only emits when newline encountered. User-facing glitch for streaming chat UX. Two separate but related parity bugs.
Samir: here's a small repro for the streaming issue — run the REST curl then the SDK stream:
```bash
# REST (streams chunks)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-3b","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat

# SDK (node)
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-3b', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }], stream: true });
stream.on('data', chunk => console.log('chunk', chunk));
```
Samir: REST prints token fragments; SDK prints only full lines.
Aj: both sound critical. We should prioritize: 1) restore `client_meta` forwarding (routing impact), 2) fix streaming behavior, 3) review auth header differences (there are reports ephemeral tokens sent as `X-Redwood-Ephemeral` by SDK but REST uses `Authorization` always).
Elyse: Proposed quick plan: patch frontend helper to keep `client_meta` for now (hotfix PR), add an SDK integration test that asserts metadata roundtrip, and open a design doc for secure metadata forwarding.
Kevin: I can own the hotfix PR and the integration test.
Kevin: assigning to myself -> will target a patch today and message rollout in #eng-releases.
Samir: I'll write the failing test case and add repro notes in the ticket.
Aj: I'll start the design doc. Need to include threat model around leaking user identifiers in `client_meta`.
Elyse: Also file a docs issue so onboarding sample app mentions streaming parity caveat until fixed. docs-bot: please create an issue.
docs-bot: [automation] Created issue RDW-1193: "docs: note SDK streaming vs REST chunking behavior in onboarding sample"
Samir: FYI — CI flaky test was failing because sample app expects immediate chunks for showing typing indicator. With SDK buffering, typing indicator waited ~1s and then appeared all at once.
Kevin: I'll add a canary in dedicated to validate routing after `client_meta` fix.
Aj: any security signoff needed for metadata whitelist change? Eng-security should be FYI.
Elyse: ping @eng-security in the PR description.
Samir: OK pushing the failing test and logs to the ticket.
Kevin: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js/pull/278 — hotfix to preserve `client_meta` in helper (will add integration test after CI green).
Elyse: nice. Once merged, we should run the onboarding e2e and verify both the routing and typing UX.
Samir: verified locally, routing now respects the client metadata. Still seeing streaming buffer — separate PR incoming.
Kevin: leaving a note in release notes draft: "fix: forward client_meta from JS helper to server to ensure routing parity with REST"
Aj: design doc link (WIP): https://docs.redwood.ai/designs/metadata-forwarding (add comments)
Elyse: thanks team. Follow-ups: add integration test, design doc, security review, docs note, and streaming fix. I'll mark this triage as P1 for DX. :white_check_mark:
Samir: thanks — will close the ticket after streaming fix is merged.
